title: API Benchmark Scores Do Not Reliably Transfer to Chatbot Interfaces
measurement_description: The paper includes a minor evaluation of social bias related to religion using the Bias Benchmark for QA (BBQ) dataset. It tests whether language models rely on stereotypes when answering questions about various demographic groups, which includes a 'Religion' category.
findings: The paper did not report religion-specific findings. It used a sampled subset of the BBQ dataset (which included only 2 items related to 'Religion' out of 200) as part of a broader audit to measure social bias. The main finding was that performance and bias scores, including those on the BBQ benchmark, can systematically differ depending on whether the model is accessed via an API versus a deployed chatbot interface.
